audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer carried a blanket "Skill" on all seven phase rows while the content layer (and the packet levelChart) read Lux/Lux/Skill/Skill/Skill/Lux/Skill. The page rendered two different answers to who wins Levels 1, 2 and First item.
audit.why: Lux Q reaches 1175 and E 1100; Galio's Q is 825 and Justice Punch 650, so at levels 1-2 she chips outside everything he owns. At Luden's her Q-E-R burst outruns his early MR stacking.
audit.corrected: full phases[0].side, phases[1].side and phases[5].side set to Lux to match win[0], win[1], win[5], which were already correct. Rows 2,3,4,6 left as Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] had 3 entries where 4 are expected; Lux's own level 6 spike was absent, so the only level-6 note on the page was Galio's Hero's Entrance.
audit.why: Final Spark is 60/50/40s at 3340 range and refreshes Illumination; it is the single largest change in Lux's lane pattern and it belongs in the spike list.
audit.corrected: Added spikes[3].text and spikes[3].when with before:null.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the decisive interaction — Justice Punch knockup chaining into the Shield of Durand taunt — was never stated. The missing-interactions file also flags that Justice Punch cuts a dashless Lux's retreat.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 at 650 range; Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14 at 275 range; Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140. Those numbers are what make the advice concrete: with E down he has no engage on Lux at all.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns with real per-rank numbers, put the E-into-W chain into enemyWin and dosFull[1].d, and put the cut-retreat point into dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under "Shield the all-in's biggest hit", and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim under "Stand at the wave's edge unshielded" (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to answer their own titles from Galio's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Colossal Smash is an auto-attack reset; the wind-up, not a cast, is the tell that the combo has started.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions (autoreset-burst-tell) and confirmed by the kit's autoReset flag on Galio's passive.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page — no field of the right length was free without displacing grounded text. Recorded here and in notes.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Prismatic Barrier has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Justice Punch (E): 11s at rank 1, 7s at rank 5 — he has no engage while it is down. - Shield of Durand (W) taunts on an 18s cooldown at rank 1. - Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1 — when it flies, that fight was decided elsewhere.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Prismatic Barrier eats one hit, so hold it for the Justice Punch knockup into the Shield of Durand taunt — not for Winds of War chip.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Justice Punch covers 650 units and knocks you up, and you have no dash — at the wave's edge with W spent, he taunts you for free.

edits.before: That is Galio’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Bait Justice Punch first; a Q into his held dash just feeds it.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Galio wins by knocking you up with Justice Punch into the Shield of Durand taunt, holding you still through every follow-up.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by punishing Hero's Entrance: he lands on your team, so bind him on arrival and laser the clump he shielded before the taunt lands.
Final Spark comes up every 60s at rank 1 and reaches 3340 units — one landed Light Binding converts into a laser Galio cannot body-block.

notes: phases[0/1/5].side moved to Lux; win[0], win[1], win[5] already read Lux, so no paired content edit was written (a no-op edit would fail the applier). The existing whys on those three rows already describe Lux winning the stage, so side and why now agree without a rewrite. spikes[2].when reads 'Rod of Ages / tank items (Galio)' — I could not verify from the kits whether Rod of Ages is still a live item on 26.15, so I left it alone. Colossal Smash's auto-reset tell is real but did not fit any field within the length band; it remains unwritten.
